raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
When decode context parallelism is enabled, the full KV cache report path used the raw physical page size from the cache spec instead of the DCP-effective block size from the manager. This caused an assertion failure in resolve_block_hashes() when a client set kv_cache_report_mode to "full" and a prefix cache hit existed, terminating the EngineCore.

Use manager.block_size (which includes DCP scaling) when emitting BlockStored events for cached prefix blocks in the full-report path.

Hit this on current `main` with `--block-size 64 --decode-context-parallel-size 8`: a `kv_cache_report_mode: "full"` request with a prefix hit asserts in `resolve_block_hashes` and stops the EngineCore. Thanks @vMaroon . Just rebased onto current `main` and moved the fix to `KVCacheCoordinator.emit_cached_block_events` (`manager.block_size` instead of the raw cache-spec page size).

Also added a regression test with `--block-size 64` / DCP 8 that asserts the full-report path no longer trips `resolve_block_hashes`, and that announced hashes match the stored prefix hashes.

We hit this on vLLM 0.31.0 with GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP8 + DCP8, and KV events enabled (Ray Serve LLM KVAwareRouter). A single request with `vllm_xargs: {"kv_cache_report_mode": "full"}` that got a prefix-cache hit killed the EngineCore with the same assert at `kv_cache_utils.py:2946`. We're blocking the field at our ingress for now. Would be great to get this reviewed and merged.
